newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks extend gains, bull run to continue.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks extend gains, bull run to continue.

text.p: Croatian stocks extended their gains on Friday after a week of steep rises in blue chips, and traders predicted the bull run would continue into next week.

"All the stocks will move upward," said one trader with a large market share, adding that the prices would continue to benefit from a positive impulse of this week's highs in market heavyweights Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka.

"Recent negotiations with the EBRD (European Bank for Reconstruction and Development) is also boosting prices," she said, referring to rumours about EBRD's plans buy into confectioner Kras and food-processing firm Podravka.
* Eight of nine active issues were up and one traded for the first time.
* Biggest gainer, hotelier Jadranturist, jumped 60 kuna to to 230 trading 760 shares.
* Most actively traded Podravka, with 5,684 shares, added another five kuna to end at 235 kuna.
* Kras closed at 470 kuna, up 40 on its steady rise, but down from a 500-kuna peak. It sold 505 shares.
* Fully-listed drugs company Pliva gained 100 kuna to 13,100 on volume of 142 units.
* Three other hoteliers were also among gainers:
- Riviera by 10 kuna to 115 on volume 653 shares
- Laguna also up 10 to 880 kuna, selling 24 and
- Suncani Hvar rose 5 kuna to 45 with 591 units sold.
* Zagrebacka Banka preferred C-series traded for the first time at 600 kuna each on volume of 83 shares.
* First issue of public debt refinancing bonds traded at 95 percent of face value, after a 12-percent interest payment, on turnover of 18.7 million.
* Volume down at 9,029 shares, but turnover almost tripled at 22.4 million kuna thanks to bonds. Weekly turnover 47.4 million kuna.
* Central bank's exchange rate: 5.3720 kuna = $1. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
